label: Performance
pick_label: The computer is slow or keeps freezing

p_start.text: Is the computer slowest right after Windows starts?
p_start.why: Slowness only at startup points to startup apps; slowness all day points to something running continuously.

p_startup.title: Turn off unneeded startup apps
p_startup.do: Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc and open Startup apps. Right-click apps you do not need at login and choose Disable, then restart. Leave security software and drivers alone.
p_startup.why: Each startup app competes for CPU, memory and disk while Windows is still loading.
p_startup.expect: Disabled apps will not open at login; you can still open them yourself.

p_done_startup.learn: Startup apps load every time you sign in. Each one uses CPU, RAM and disk, so a long list slows the first minutes of every session.

p_taskmgr.title: Find what is using your resources
p_taskmgr.do: Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc and open Processes. Click the CPU, Memory and Disk headings to sort. If one ordinary app uses most of a resource, save your work and close it.
p_taskmgr.why: This shows which resource is the bottleneck.
p_taskmgr.expect: The busiest apps appear at the top of the list.

p_done_taskmgr.cause: One app or background process using most of the CPU, memory or disk.
p_done_taskmgr.learn: Task Manager shows CPU, RAM and disk use per process. A single runaway process can slow the whole system.

p_disk.text: Open File Explorer > This PC. Does the C: drive have less than 10% free space?
p_disk.why: Windows needs free space for temporary files and virtual memory.

p_space.caution: Removed temporary files cannot be restored. Leave Downloads unticked unless you have checked it.
p_space.title: Free up disk space
p_space.do: Open Settings > System > Storage. Turn on Storage Sense or open Temporary files and remove what you do not need. Leave Downloads unticked unless you have checked it.
p_space.why: A nearly full drive slows saving, loading and virtual memory.
p_space.expect: The amount of free space increases.

p_done_space.learn: When RAM runs short, Windows uses disk space as virtual memory. If the disk is nearly full, that fallback is slow or unavailable.

p_hot.text: Does the computer feel very hot, or is the fan loud all the time?
p_hot.why: Hot processors slow themselves down to protect themselves.

p_vent.caution: Let it cool down first and keep the case closed. Do not open the laptop.
p_vent.title: Improve airflow
p_vent.do: Shut down, unplug and let it cool. Use it on a hard, flat surface and make sure the air vents are not blocked. Gently clear dust from the outside vents with a soft brush. Do not open the case.
p_vent.why: Restricted airflow makes the processor slow down (thermal throttling).
p_vent.expect: It should run cooler and the fan should be quieter.

p_done_vent.learn: Processors reduce their speed when they get too hot. Blocked vents and soft surfaces such as beds trap heat.

p_restart.title: Restart the computer
p_restart.why: A restart clears temporary software problems that build up over days.
p_restart.expect: The computer restarts and may feel faster.

p_done_restart.learn: Memory leaks and stuck processes build up over time. A restart resets them.

p_pro_heat.reason: Overheating that continues after safe airflow checks may need a technician to inspect the fan and cooling system. FixWise AI does not guide internal cleaning or repair.
causes: Dust built up inside the device

p_pro_perf.reason: The safe checks are used up. Lasting slowness can have deeper causes, such as a failing drive or too little RAM, that need further testing.
causes: Too little memory (RAM) for the workload
